Query MongoDB as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__mongodb.R
oauth_db_mongodb.Rd

Read MongoDB collections, run aggregation pipelines and issue database commands using the visitor's OAuth access token. Uses the official PyMongo driver through reticulate, with a separate client for each Shiny session.

Usage

oauth_db_mongodb(
  authorization,
  url,
  db,
  issuer,
  user = NULL,
  client_id = NULL,
  allowed_hosts = NULL,
  timeout = 30,
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

url

Credential-free mongodb:// or mongodb+srv:// connection URL. Authentication, TLS, retry and timeout options are set by the helper.

db

Database name.

issuer

Exact HTTPS issuer configured for MongoDB workforce OIDC.

user

Optional MongoDB OIDC username, or a function returning it. Useful when the deployment uses the username to select an identity provider.

client_id

Optional expected client ID in MongoDB's OIDC challenge.

allowed_hosts

Hostnames to which PyMongo may send visitor tokens. An entry can start with *. to allow subdomains. Defaults to the seed hosts for ordinary URLs, or the cluster's parent domain for Atlas SRV URLs. Supply this explicitly for other SRV deployments or additional replica hosts.

timeout

Positive operation timeout in seconds, including server selection, authentication and fetching result pages.

ca_bundle

Optional trusted CA certificate file. TLS always verifies certificates and hostnames.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A client with these methods:

  • $find(collection, filter = "{}", projection = "{\"_id\":0}", sort = "{}", skip = 0, limit = 100, simplify = TRUE) reads documents.

  • $aggregate(collection, pipeline, simplify = TRUE) consumes an aggregation cursor, including all result pages.

  • $count(collection, filter = "{}") counts matching documents.

  • $run(command, simplify = FALSE) issues one database command. Authentication, transaction and cursor commands are excluded.

Inputs use MongoDB JSON or Extended JSON strings. Reads return data frames by default; simplify = FALSE preserves lists. BSON-specific values retain their Extended JSON representation, and large integers remain strings.

Details

MongoDB must support workforce OIDC: Atlas with workforce federation, or a supported Linux MongoDB Enterprise deployment. Community Server doesn't provide this authentication. Configure the issuer, audience and database user or group permissions before connecting.

Install reticulate and PyMongo 4.10 or later in its selected Python environment. Python is initialized only on the first signed-in operation; the helper never installs dependencies or chooses a different interpreter. mongolite currently has no public OIDC callback for supplying visitor tokens.

Create the client inside server(). shinyOAuth obtains and renews tokens. PyMongo's human OIDC callback supplies only the current client's access token after checking the server's issuer and optional client ID. It never starts browser sign-in or uses workload credentials from the app host.

Clients are replaced on their next use after token or username changes. Sign-out, permission loss and session end close them. Results arriving after an authorization change are discarded. Cursors are consumed and closed in the operation that created them; transactions and retained cursors aren't exposed. limit = 0 fetches all matching documents.

Driver retryable reads and writes are disabled, and the helper doesn't replay failed operations. PyMongo handles protocol reauthentication with the same supplied token. A failed or timed-out operation can still have effects on the server, including aggregation pipelines that write data.

See also

vignette("mongodb", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
mongo <- oauth_db_mongodb(auth$connection,
  url = "mongodb://mongo.example.org:27017", db = "reporting",
  issuer = "https://login.example.org/realms/reporting")
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  mongo$find("orders", filter = '{"country":"NL"}', limit = 20)
})
} # }
